description: Global seismicity of the last 30 days, read as remote GeoParquet by DuckDB. The map holds every event and its time slider narrows what is drawn; the summary and the table below follow that window through two dashboard variables rather than through the dashboard time range.

panels.description: Time range sync is set to `variables`, not `toMap`. Moving the dashboard range would re-run this query, and every event outside the new range would leave the browser — the histogram under the slider would rescale and the window could never be widened again from the map. Publishing the window to variables instead keeps the whole month loaded and costs only the panels that read them. Clicking the map publishes the place to $​lat/$​lng (a Coordinates mapping); DuckDB builds a geodesic circle of $​radio km around it (query B) and intersects the quakes with it (query C), which come back as the coverage outline and a magnitude-weighted heatmap.

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET force_download = true;

-- force_download is not tuning. This endpoint builds the parquet per request,
-- so each ranged read sees a different ETag and DuckDB aborts with "the remote
-- file has changed". One whole-file GET sidesteps it; at 378 KB that is free.
SELECT
  place,
  mag,
  depth_num               AS depth,
  event_time_utc_date_fmt AS time,
  latitude_num            AS latitude,
  longitude_num           AS longitude
FROM read_parquet('https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/datasets/2717becb-bfc5-4029-845f-24c3bbe19780/export?format=parquet')

INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;

-- The coverage circle around the click ($lat/$lng, radius $radio km), drawn
-- by the pinned geojson layer. A true geodesic ring — the spherical
-- destination formula per bearing — because ST_Buffer is planar and in
-- degrees, which at these radii draws an ellipse. Both variables empty (no
-- click yet) returns no rows and no circle.
WITH params AS (
  SELECT try_cast($lat AS DOUBLE) AS lat0,
         try_cast($lng AS DOUBLE) AS lng0,
         coalesce(try_cast($radio AS DOUBLE), 500) / 6371.0 AS d
),
pts AS (
  SELECT deg,
         asin(sin(radians(lat0)) * cos(d) + cos(radians(lat0)) * sin(d) * cos(radians(deg))) AS lat2,
         lat0, lng0, d
  FROM params, (SELECT unnest(generate_series(0, 360, 6)) AS deg)
  WHERE lat0 IS NOT NULL AND lng0 IS NOT NULL
),
ring AS (
  SELECT deg,
         degrees(lat2) AS lat_deg,
         lng0 + degrees(atan2(sin(radians(deg)) * sin(d) * cos(radians(lat0)),
                              cos(d) - sin(radians(lat0)) * sin(lat2))) AS lng_deg
  FROM pts
)
SELECT
  ST_AsHEXWKB(ST_GeomFromText(
    'POLYGON((' || string_agg(round(lng_deg, 5) || ' ' || round(lat_deg, 5), ',' ORDER BY deg) || '))'
  )) AS geom,
  'radio' AS name
FROM ring
HAVING count(*) > 0

INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;
SET force_download = true;

-- The quakes inside the click's circle, for the pinned heatmap layer. The
-- ring is regenerated identical to query B's, so what the heatmap counts is
-- exactly what the drawn circle encloses; the time window follows the map's
-- slider through the same variable pair the other panels read.
WITH params AS (
  SELECT try_cast($lat AS DOUBLE) AS lat0,
         try_cast($lng AS DOUBLE) AS lng0,
         coalesce(try_cast($radio AS DOUBLE), 500) / 6371.0 AS d
),
pts AS (
  SELECT deg,
         asin(sin(radians(lat0)) * cos(d) + cos(radians(lat0)) * sin(d) * cos(radians(deg))) AS lat2,
         lat0, lng0, d
  FROM params, (SELECT unnest(generate_series(0, 360, 6)) AS deg)
  WHERE lat0 IS NOT NULL AND lng0 IS NOT NULL
),
ring AS (
  SELECT deg,
         degrees(lat2) AS lat_deg,
         lng0 + degrees(atan2(sin(radians(deg)) * sin(d) * cos(radians(lat0)),
                              cos(d) - sin(radians(lat0)) * sin(lat2))) AS lng_deg
  FROM pts
),
circle AS (
  SELECT ST_GeomFromText(
    'POLYGON((' || string_agg(round(lng_deg, 5) || ' ' || round(lat_deg, 5), ',' ORDER BY deg) || '))'
  ) AS geom
  FROM ring
  HAVING count(*) > 0
)
SELECT
  latitude_num  AS latitude,
  longitude_num AS longitude,
  mag
FROM read_parquet('https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/datasets/2717becb-bfc5-4029-845f-24c3bbe19780/export?format=parquet'), circle
WHERE ST_Contains(circle.geom, ST_Point(longitude_num, latitude_num))
  AND event_time_utc_date_fmt
    BETWEEN COALESCE(try_cast($quakeFrom AS TIMESTAMPTZ), '-infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
        AND COALESCE(try_cast($quakeTo   AS TIMESTAMPTZ), 'infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)

panels.title: Global seismicity — the last 30 days

panels.description: Reads the map's window. Both variables start empty — before the slider has been touched — so each bound falls back to an infinity, and the summary covers everything rather than nothing.

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;
SET force_download = true;

SELECT
  count(*)                 AS "Sismos",
  round(max(mag), 1)       AS "Magnitud máxima",
  round(avg(depth_num), 1) AS "Profundidad media (km)"
FROM read_parquet('https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/datasets/2717becb-bfc5-4029-845f-24c3bbe19780/export?format=parquet')
WHERE event_time_utc_date_fmt
  BETWEEN COALESCE(try_cast($quakeFrom AS TIMESTAMPTZ), '-infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
      AND COALESCE(try_cast($quakeTo   AS TIMESTAMPTZ), 'infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
  -- The drawn area arrives as WKT via $quakeArea; empty means no spatial cut.
  AND ($quakeArea = '' OR ST_Contains(ST_GeomFromText($quakeArea), ST_Point(longitude_num, latitude_num)))

panels.title: Inside the map's window

panels.description: The ten strongest events inside the map's window. Scrub the slider and this list follows. Clicking a row writes the quake's coordinates to $​lat/$​lng: the map centres there (the Center mapping) and the coverage circle and heatmap recompute around it.

links.title: Centrar el mapa en este sismo

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;
SET force_download = true;

-- latitude/longitude are hidden in the table; they feed the row's data link,
-- which writes them to $lat/$lng so the map centres on the clicked quake.
SELECT
  strftime(event_time_utc_date_fmt, '%d %b %H:%M') AS "Fecha",
  place                                            AS "Lugar",
  mag                                              AS "Mag",
  latitude_num                                     AS latitude,
  longitude_num                                    AS longitude
FROM read_parquet('https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/datasets/2717becb-bfc5-4029-845f-24c3bbe19780/export?format=parquet')
WHERE event_time_utc_date_fmt
  BETWEEN COALESCE(try_cast($quakeFrom AS TIMESTAMPTZ), '-infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
      AND COALESCE(try_cast($quakeTo   AS TIMESTAMPTZ), 'infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
  -- The drawn area arrives as WKT via $quakeArea; empty means no spatial cut.
  AND ($quakeArea = '' OR ST_Contains(ST_GeomFromText($quakeArea), ST_Point(longitude_num, latitude_num)))
ORDER BY mag DESC
LIMIT 10

panels.title: The strongest in the window

panels.description: Deliberately unfiltered: this is the context the slider moves through, so it must show the whole month whatever the window is.

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET force_download = true;

SELECT
  date_trunc('day', event_time_utc_date_fmt) AS time,
  count(*)           AS "Sismos",
  round(max(mag), 1) AS "Magnitud máxima"
FROM read_parquet('https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/datasets/2717becb-bfc5-4029-845f-24c3bbe19780/export?format=parquet')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
